item.text:
I used the local prior as the base and did not re-fetch structured datasets already supplied there. I also did not use the client matrix. This is research-only, no scoring.

**Bottom Line**
Xi Jinping in 2022 held the core office bundle of CCP General Secretary, PRC President, and CMC Chairman. The strongest 2022 evidence shows a high degree of personal concentration of authority through the 20th Party Congress, but also real constraints: elite/state implementation bottlenecks, zero-COVID backlash, economic slowdown, and sustained external human-rights criticism. That last point is an inference from the source set, not a single source claim.

**Retained Sources**
1. [党的二十届一中全会产生中央领导机构习近平任中共中央总书记中央军委主席](https://cpc.people.com.cn/20th/gb/n1/2022/1024/c448334-32550105.html) - People’s Daily / People.cn, Oct. 24, 2022.  
   Precise fact: the Chinese-language party press lists Xi as CPC General Secretary and CMC Chairman in the new leadership lineup.  
   Period fit: exact office confirmation immediately after the 20th Party Congress.  
   Ruler attribution: official self-description of the regime’s top offices.  
   Limitations: celebratory framing, no independent corroboration.  
   Contrary point: confirms title, not the practical ceiling on power.

2. [Full text of resolution on Party Constitution amendment](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/topnews/202210/22/content_WS6353e0bbc6d0a757729e18c7.html) - gov.cn / Xinhua, Oct. 22, 2022.  
   Precise fact: the revised CPC constitution incorporates Xi Jinping Thought and reaffirms Xi’s “core” position.  
   Period fit: direct evidence from the congress at the moment of rule consolidation.  
   Ruler attribution: highly authoritative, but normative and self-justifying.  
   Limitations: party text, not an external measurement.  
   Contrary point: ideological elevation is not the same as unconstrained personal discretion.

3. [Full text of the report to the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/topnews/202210/25/content_WS6357df20c6d0a757729e1bfc.html) - gov.cn / Xinhua, Oct. 25, 2022.  
   Precise fact: Xi’s congress report sets out the 2022 governing agenda, including “high-quality development” and a more assertive domestic/international policy line.  
   Period fit: primary statement of direction for the year’s decisive political pivot.  
   Ruler attribution: Xi is the report’s author and presenter.  
   Limitations: aspiration-heavy; success and implementation are separate questions.  
   Contrary point: the report reveals priorities more than outcomes.

4. [Communique of the first plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/topnews/202210/24/content_WS6355cfccc6d0a757729e19b4.html) - gov.cn / Xinhua, Oct. 24, 2022.  
   Precise fact: Xi is reaffirmed in the new central leadership, including the top party-military bundle.  
   Period fit: confirms continuity of office after the congress.  
   Ruler attribution: strongest formal confirmation of post-congress leadership.  
   Limitations: official communique; no dissent or contestation.  
   Contrary point: strong title continuity does not itself measure effective implementation.

5. [China's Xi clinches third term, packs leadership with loyalists](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/chinas-xi-clinches-third-term-packs-leadership-with-loyalists-2919033) - Reuters, Oct. 23, 2022.  
   Precise fact: Xi secures a precedent-breaking third term and the top body is filled with loyalists.  
   Period fit: independent confirmation of the congress outcome.  
   Ruler attribution: links the office change to Xi’s own consolidation.  
   Limitations: news framing, not a legal text.  
   Contrary point: “loyalists” describes political composition, not formal powers.

6. [China tightens security after rare protests against COVID curbs](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/china-reports-another-daily-record-of-covid-cases-as-protests-ripple-across-china-2952419) - Reuters, Nov. 27, 2022.  
   Precise fact: protests against COVID restrictions spread across cities and campuses; security tightened.  
   Period fit: captures the major late-2022 constraint on Xi’s governance.  
   Ruler attribution: directly tied to frustration with Xi’s signature zero-COVID policy.  
   Limitations: urban protest coverage is necessarily partial.  
   Contrary point: protests indicate pressure on policy, not regime collapse.

7. [China set to loosen COVID curbs after week of historic protests](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/china-set-to-loosen-covid-curbs-after-week-of-historic-protests-2955191) - Reuters, Dec. 1, 2022.  
   Precise fact: Reuters reports imminent national easing of quarantine and mass-testing rules after unrest.  
   Period fit: key transition from hard zero-COVID toward rollback.  
   Ruler attribution: useful for showing the policy shift that Xi had to absorb.  
   Limitations: sources-based reporting during a rapidly changing policy moment.  
   Contrary point: the easing did not instantly end the wider zero-COVID apparatus.

8. [China Focus: COVID-19 response further optimized with 10 new measures](https://english.news.cn/20221207/ca014c043bf24728b8dcbc0198565fdf/c.html) - Xinhua, Dec. 7, 2022.  
   Precise fact: the State Council mechanism released 10 measures to relax and refine COVID controls.  
   Period fit: official record of the December policy turn.  
   Ruler attribution: official regime response to pressure, showing constraint and adaptation.  
   Limitations: favorable framing; no discussion of policy failure costs.  
   Contrary point: the text presents optimization, but the move itself signals prior strain.

9. [Human Rights Reports: Custom Report Excerpts: China, Hong Kong, Macau, and Tibet](https://2021-2025.state.gov/report/custom/2bf7da2efe/) - U.S. State Department, 2023 report covering 2022.  
   Precise fact: the report describes the CCP as paramount authority and says Xi held the three most powerful positions.  
   Period fit: excellent for formal authority and institutional constraint language.  
   Ruler attribution: directly names Xi’s office bundle.  
   Limitations: U.S. government perspective and broad country scope.  
   Contrary point: formal institutional descriptions do not fully capture informal personal power.

10. [IMF Staff Completes 2022 Article IV Mission to the People’s Republic of China](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2022/11/21/pr22401-imf-staff-completes-2022-article-iv-mission-to-the-peoples-republic-of-china) - IMF, Nov. 23, 2022.  
   Precise fact: IMF staff said growth had slowed and was under pressure from zero-COVID and the property sector.  
   Period fit: strong inherited-condition source for the 2022 environment.  
   Ruler attribution: macro pressure on Xi’s governing agenda, not personal conduct.  
   Limitations: forecast-based and macro-focused.  
   Contrary point: it measures the economy, not ruler intent.

11. [National Economy Withstood Pressure and Reached a New Level in 2022](https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202301/t20230117_1892094.html) - National Bureau of Statistics of China, Jan. 17, 2023, reporting 2022 official results.  
   Precise fact: official GDP growth for 2022 was 3.0 percent, with Q4 slower than earlier quarters.  
   Period fit: direct official reading on 2022 macro conditions.  
   Ruler attribution: inherited economic conditions during Xi’s rule, not a ruler-quality score.  
   Limitations: official statistics may be politically managed.  
   Contrary point: still the standard official series and useful as the regime’s own baseline.

12. [China Military Power Report Examines Changes in Beijing's Strategy](https://www.defense.gov/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/3230682/china-military-power-report-examines-changes-in-beijings-strategy/) - U.S. Department of Defense, Nov. 29, 2022.  
   Precise fact: the 2022 China Military Power Report describes China’s strategic/military modernization and expanding ambitions.  
   Period fit: best retained source for 1B-style military context in 2022.  
   Ruler attribution: relevant to Xi because the PLA is central to his power base and foreign-policy leverage.  
   Limitations: U.S. defense perspective, strategic lens, and capability estimates carry uncertainty.  
   Contrary point: modernization trends are not identical to operational performance or responsible use.

**Compact Event Map**
- April 2022: Shanghai lockdown becomes a vivid symbol of zero-COVID stress and implementation cost.
- August 31, 2022: OHCHR releases its Xinjiang assessment, intensifying external human-rights pressure.
- October 16-24, 2022: 20th Party Congress, Xi’s congress report, constitution amendment, and confirmation of his third-term leadership.
- Late November 2022: rare protests against COVID controls spread across cities and campuses.
- December 7, 2022: official rollback begins with 10 new COVID measures.
- December 2022: the policy shift continues amid concern about infections and economic damage.
- 2022 as a whole: growth slows sharply under the combined weight of zero-COVID, property weakness, and weaker external demand.

**Chapter Source Plan**
- 1B: Use [DoD CMPR](https://www.defense.gov/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/3230682/china-military-power-report-examines-changes-in-beijings-strategy/) plus SIPRI/IISS later if you need fuller force-capability saturation.
- 2B: Use Reuters protest/easing coverage plus the official Xinhua COVID-measures pages; the local prior already covers the structured conflict and military-spend baselines.
- 3B: Use OHCHR, the State Department human-rights report, and Reuters protest coverage; the local prior already covers the country-year repression indicators.
- 4B: Use the party congress report, constitution amendment resolution, first plenary communique, and Reuters third-term coverage.
- 5B: Use IMF and NBS for the inherited macro setting, with the congress report for policy direction.
- 6B: Use NBS, IMF, and the December COVID-policy sources for the health/welfare backdrop.
- 7B: Use the constitution amendment resolution, State Department report, and OHCHR for corruption/accountability/rule-of-law context, with the local prior for the structured institutional indicators.
- 8B: Use the congress report, first plenary communique, IMF, and NBS for state-capacity and implementation context.
